title: Prioritize customer-requested quantized model variants and pin cadence playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for customer requests that ask for quantized (lower-precision) model variants, including rules for version pinning cadence, automated evaluation gates, and rollback conditions. This ticket creates the product-side rubric, Console UX changes required for pin lifecycle, and the operational steps for safe canary rollouts for enterprise customers who demand quantized variants for cost/performance reasons.
background: Several enterprise customers have asked for officially cataloged quantized variants (e.g., int8/4-bit) of mainstream models to reduce cost and improve throughput in Dedicated and Private deployments. Quantized variants can introduce subtle quality regressions (formatting, hallucination, or safety) that are sensitive to prompt distribution. We lack a standardized intake path and lifecycle for pinning quantized variants to customer workloads and for periodically re-evaluating pins after upstream model updates or new quantization kernels.
proposed_solution: Add explicit intake fields in the model-request form: desired quantization (e.g., fp16, int8, q4f16), priority of CPU/GPU savings vs. fidelity, and a sponsor for enterprise requests.
Implement a triage rubric that scores requests by business impact, expected token-volume savings, regression risk (based on eval suites), and compliance constraints.

Introduce an automated eval-gate job that runs candidate quantized variants on a customer-subset of representative prompts; gates include pass/fail on exact-match tasks, response-quality thresholds, and hallucination/safety regressions.
Design Console pin lifecycle UI additions: pin reason, pin start/end dates (auto-expiry), cadence policy (auto-retest every N weeks), and one-click rollback to previous full-precision variant.

Productionize a canary rollout path: traffic split knob in Console (1% → 10% → 50%), progressive telemetry checks (latency, top-k token divergence, downstream metric regressions), and automatic rollback triggers.
Create an internal runbook mapping pin states to required communication with customer success (e.g., when auto-retest fails) and legal if compliance flags appear.
Capture metrics for economics: per-token cost delta, throughput improvements, and SLO impact for pinned quantized variants.
Add a periodic pin-cadence policy default (90 days) with an opt-in faster cadence for high-frequency updates (30 days) and a freeze window for enterprise audit periods.
Work with Engineering to add telemetry hooks for token-level divergence and end-to-end eval throughput to feed the automated eval-gate service.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated and available in staging with quantization-specific fields and sponsor capture
Triage rubric documented in Confluence and used in two pilot requests
Automated eval-gate runs end-to-end in staging with pass/fail outputs and sample artifacts stored
Console shows pin metadata (reason, expiry, cadence) and can trigger staged traffic-split rollouts
Runbook exists and CS/SE team trained on communications and rollback expectations
Pilot with one enterprise customer completes canary rollout and publishes post-mortem noting costs, quality deltas, and cadence recommendation
steps: Draft updated intake form and share with Solutions Engineering for feedback (Mar 2–Mar 6)
Build triage rubric and scoring spreadsheet; run retrospective on historical requests to calibrate thresholds (Mar 8–Mar 12)
Coordinate with Eng to prototype an eval-gate job using existing eval infra; define metric thresholds (Mar 15–Mar 22)
Design Console pin metadata UI and rollout control wireframes; review with Design (DES) and Security (Mar 18–Mar 24)
Run pilot canary with two internal workloads, then with one consenting customer (Apr 1–Apr 12)
Iterate on defaults for pin-cadence and expiry based on pilot results, update docs and training materials (Apr 13–Apr 20)
Ship release catalog-2026.04 with feature flags and monitored rollout (Apr 26)
Measure first-month economics and QA metrics; prepare executive summary for PM leadership (May 26)
Post-mortem and next-steps decision: general availability or additional constraints (May 30)
If GA: add to model onboarding checklist and public catalog metadata
out_of_scope: This ticket does not include building new quantization kernels or low-level runtime changes; ENG ownership is limited to telemetry and eval-gate plumbing. It also does not include pricing policy changes—pricing decisions will be a separate commercial ticket.
